claims.claim: Linear probes on LLaDA-8B and Dream-7B hidden states predict functional correctness; step-0 signal is comparable to an AR Qwen-2.5-7B last-prompt-token probe, so it reflects prompt difficulty.
claims.stance_target: L2: hidden-state correctness probes with MBPP exist only for diffusion LMs, one of four tasks
claims.scope_conditions: Full text read from the ACL Anthology PDF (curl into scratchpad); vault note is ABSTRACT-ONLY because the CLI rejected the PDF as junk
claims.quoted_support: Sec 6: An AR baseline probe on Qwen-2.5-7B's last prompt token achieves comparable AUC on most tasks (Appendix F), suggesting that much of the step-0 signal reflects prompt difficulty detectable by any model.

claims.claim: Probe confidence for selective generation saves 36-98% of denoising compute in an offline simulation (tau=0.80); on MBPP LLaDA saves 95.5% and Dream 97.8%, with classifier accuracy 66.5% and 70.0% against majority 59.1% and 55.6%.
claims.stance_target: L3: probe-routed compute saving exists for MBPP in DLMs (simulation, not execution budget)
claims.quoted_support: Table 2: LLaDA MBPP Compute saved 95.5%, Clf. accuracy 66.5%, Majority acc. 59.1%; Dream MBPP 97.8%, 70.0%, 55.6%

claims.claim: The probe outperforms raw softmax entropy and max-prob baselines by 5-20 pp classification accuracy at tau=0.80, and a text-feature probe in 7 of 8 settings.
claims.quoted_support: Sec 5.3: the probe outperforms the best raw signal in classification accuracy at tau = 0.80 by 5-20 percentage points

claims.claim: Probes use PCA to 64 components and logistic regression with 5-fold CV; shuffled-label controls give AUC 0.53-0.58 versus 0.65-0.88 real; MBPP has 257 sanitized test instances.
claims.quoted_support: Sec 3: shuffled-label controls yield 0.53-0.58 across all eight (dataset, model) settings, well below the actual probe AUCs of 0.65-0.88
